new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote: both segments of the reported quote are verbatim in, lines 5440-5443 ('Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior.') and lines 5490-5491 ('In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec.'); extracted text of the PDF confirms this is PDF page 108 = printed p. 86, section 4.2.1, exactly as the locator says (the '[..]' is the reader's elision of the intervening per-variety survey: Ayutla, Jicaltepec, Acatlan, Diuxi, Mixtepec, Atatlahuca, Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala -- n…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Pan-Mixtec generalization (Josserand's dialect survey, which includes Santa Cruz Itundujia among its 122 towns): the root/stem 'couplet' is disyllabic (bimoraic) and stress falls on its first syllable, i.e. the penultimate syllable of the couplet; no Itundujia-specific stress description exists.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Itundujia. Carroll notes (pp. 86-87) that in some varieties (Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala, Atatlahuca) vocalic enclitics shift the computation, and that Yoloxochitl Mixtec has been described with final stress -- none of this concerns Itundujia.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the lexical couplet (disyllabic/bimoraic root or stem), not the phonological word with clitics/prefixes; statement is a survey-wide generalization by Josserand, reported second-hand by Carroll. Itundujia's own data in circulation is only Josserand's 188-item wordlist, untonemarked and without stress marks.
new_statements.identity_note: No source describes Itundujia Mixtec (itun1239, mce) itself. The only stress statement whose scope covers it is Josserand's (1983:180) survey-wide generalization over all Mixtec varieties (Santa Cruz Itundujia = Josserand town code 'Itun', Carroll 2015 Table A.2, group Alta:W; Auderset et al. subgroup 6.2.2 Western Alta; Glottolog Chalcatongic). The variety is reported moribund (Julián Caballero 2009 lists Itundujia among communities that no longer speak Mixtec), which is consistent with the total absence of dedicated documentation.
